RESEARCH UPDATED · NOVEMBER 20, 2026

Start with the Roku Streaming Stick 4K 3820 family if Dolby Vision or HDR10+ matters to your TV setup. The older Streaming Stick+ 3810 is worth comparing when a complete kit costs meaningfully less. Check the model number and supplied equipment before choosing between them.

Roku Streaming Stick 4K: start here for the broader HDR formats

The 3820 family makes the clearer starting point when your TV and usual content support Dolby Vision or HDR10+. A player cannot add those capabilities to an incompatible display, and a 4K badge is not evidence that every program or subscription streams in 4K.

Why consider it: the supported HDR formats fit your display and viewing habits. Drawback: those features offer less benefit on an ordinary HD screen; compare the full kit price rather than paying for labels you will not use.

Roku Streaming Stick+: compare the older 3810 kit carefully

The 3810 supports 4K and HDR10, but it is a different product from the newer 3830 Streaming Stick Plus. Roku currently lists 3810 among its updatable models, rather than current production. That status does not promise a future support period for the device or every app.

Why consider it: a complete, working older kit may suit an HDR10 setup if the saving is worthwhile. Drawback: missing equipment, weaker return terms or a small saving can make an older offer poor value. Do not assume the photographs include everything supplied.

The power cable is part of the working setup

For both model families, Roku places the wireless receiver in the supplied USB cable. A generic charging cable is therefore not automatically a usable substitute. Before buying an open-box or used unit, confirm the correct receiver cable, power equipment and compatible remote are included. Roku recommends wall power where a TV's USB port cannot provide enough power.

Check the service you actually want to watch

Confirm that your intended apps work on the exact model in the USA, and check any subscription charges separately. Compare the usable kit, not a remote, cable or replacement part that merely mentions Roku. If your existing TV already runs the services you use reliably, an extra streaming player may solve no practical problem.

How we researched this comparison

We checked the linked Roku specifications and setup guidance on November 20, 2026. This is a researched buying comparison, not our own hands-on performance test. We do not quote a current deal price or assign a performance score to these model searches. Confirm the exact hardware generation, live price and seller's return policy before ordering.
